newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht surges offshore to new 13-year high.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht surges offshore to new 13-year high.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied in the offshore market to a new 13-year high on Tuesday against the dollar on heavy demand ahead of the maturity of more baht/dollar forward contracts abroad, dealers said.
Offshore players, facing a severe shortage of baht after the last speculative attack on the Thai unit in mid-May, sold dollars at a high premium to acquire baht, they added.

The baht was quoted at 23.460/24.560 to the dollar early in offshore market, the highest level since the last baht devaluation in 1984. The baht was traded at 24.250/24.300 late on Monday in the offshore market.
"There are a lot of maturities (of one-month forward contracts made during the last baht attack) coming up. Everybody is going through it," said one Singapore-based dealer.

Dealers said costly baht/dollar swap premiums and the Bank of Thailand's strict controls to cut off baht supply to offshore parties also forced them to unwind dollar positions in the spot market for the baht.
"There are not many channels (to get the baht) right now. So many tried to get it in the spot market," another dealer said.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium rallied to 165/185 satangs per dollar offshore early from 100/110 late on Monday.
The spread was wide between baht values in the offshore and onshore markets.
In the onshore domestic market, the baht firmed to 25.800/25.810 from 25.835/25.845 late on Monday in line with the U.S. unit's weakness abroad, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.77 per dollar versus 25.81 on Monday.
The one-month swap premium was quoted at 15/20 satangs here compared with 14.00/19.00 late on Monday.
The overnight interbank rate edged up to 13.00-14.00 percent early from 12.50-12.75 late on Monday on tighter liquidity, dealers said.-- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
